links.title: MC Overview
links.tooltip: Joins, security events, GC/Redis, and MH Coordination incl. meeting teardown (EndMeeting outcomes, push quiesce, fence backstop).

panels.description: Forwarding-policy pushes to an MH, by what the handler's reply proved (ADR-0036 §8). THIS IS THE DETECTION SIGNAL for a meeting whose policy MC could not confirm as live. Counts response evaluations, NOT meetings: a retried push contributes one sample per attempt. A reply from a DIFFERENT handler incarnation (an in-place MH restart) is never classified here - it is mc_register_meeting_total{status="handler_replaced"} (story 4 MC-B1, ADR-0039 §7) - so every non-match outcome is a real divergence and the alert reads outcome!="match". Live per-(meeting, handler) lag is Handler Applied-Sequence Lag below. No meeting identifier, sender id or generation number appears as a label. COLOUR: red is the three Err outcomes; the red regexp is anchored so a later outcome whose name contains "mismatch" cannot silently join the red set.
panels.title: Media Policy Pushes by Outcome

panels.description: The exact selector of MCMediaGenerationDivergence (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml): every policy push outcome that is not a confirmed match, NEGATED so an outcome added later is drawn here. The rule pages on ANY occurrence in 15 minutes; any point above the red line at 0 is such an occurrence. Since story 3 transport_mode_mismatch is per stream (arm and first stream on MC's confirm-failure ERROR line). Split by outcome on Media Policy Pushes by Outcome; the live per-(meeting, handler) lag is Handler Applied-Sequence Lag. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Pushes Counted by MCMediaGenerationDivergence (ALERTED, page)

panels.description: Whether MC could resolve a participant's sender_id for the Media Handler that asked, and if not why (ADR-0036 §2, §4; R-15). Increments once per NotifyParticipantConnected RESPONSE MC emits. READ THIS BEFORE COMPARING WITH MH: MH sees only sender_id==0 and structurally cannot tell the three unresolved outcomes apart - its declined_no_sender_binding is the UNION of all three. This panel is the only place the split exists, and the outcomes triage differently: meeting_unknown is a routing/registration fault whose remedy is in the MC-MH registration path; participant_unknown is an expected low-rate race between MH's connect notification and MC's join completing; registry_full is RETIRED (story 2 task 20: the connection registry and its cap are gone; MC never declines a binding for capacity) - a non-zero value can only come from an MC image predating the retirement during a rolling deploy, version skew, NOT a capacity signal; user_ambiguous is one user with two roster entries for one sub, which NEVER self-clears and which RECONNECTING CAUSES - so the participant_unknown remedy (reconnect) is actively HARMFUL here and there is no operator remedy (full triage in mh-incident-response.md Scenario 15 Step 2). connection_id does NOT resolve it: it tells MH connections apart, not MC joins (docs/TODO.md, 'user_ambiguous has no operator remedy'). THE sender_id VALUE IS NEVER A LABEL (ADR-0036 §11): outcome carries the triage signal as a bounded token instead of one value per sender_id in the u16 namespace. No meeting id, participant id or sender id appears as a label. DENOMINATOR NOTE: sum() over this metric equals mc_mh_notifications_received_total{event_type="connected"} by construction - same path, same gate - so do not alert on both as if they were independent.
panels.title: Sender Binding Responses by Outcome

panels.description: MC-restart generation floors (mc_media_policy_generation_adoptions_total): a restarted MC's FIRST push to a live handler was answered with a higher applied generation (the pre-restart MC's number), and MC adopted it as a floor and re-pushed above it. SPLIT BY outcome: adopted is the recovery event, EXPECTED during an MC rollout at most one per live (meeting, handler); superseded is routine coalescing (a restart-floor reply discarded for a newer render, no adoption, no per-pair bound). A rising adopted count a rise with NO MC restart is not - investigate as a second MC programming the same meeting (MC runbook Scenario 15). Recorded HERE INSTEAD of Media Policy Pushes{outcome=generation_mismatch}, so this arm is deliberately invisible under every outcome label and MCMediaGenerationDivergence does not page on rollouts; a FAILED adoption, or any higher echo after a confirm, is still recorded as generation_mismatch and pages. Total evaluated replies = pushes + adoptions. Zero is healthy; an ABSENT series is NOT a zero - it means the metrics pipeline is broken.
panels.title: Policy Generation Floor Adoptions

panels.description: Client receive-capability declarations by disposition (ADR-0036 §6). This metric PARTITIONS declarations: every one lands in exactly one bucket. THE SUCCESS SET IS {accepted, accepted_unchanged}, so the complete rejection count is outcome!~"accepted|accepted_unchanged". DO NOT USE outcome!="accepted": that counts a success as a rejection, and the success it counts is the one value a client can inflate for free. USE accepted ALONE AS ANY RATIO DENOMINATOR - accepted_unchanged is an identical re-declaration that MC does no work for, so it is client-inflatable at near-zero server cost and a ratio computed over it is an evadable alert. Rejection is always WHOLE-DECLARATION - MC never accepts a prefix, never applies last-write-wins to a duplicate, never clamps an out-of-range id. COLOUR, and read it carefully: GREEN is accepted; DARK GREEN is accepted_unchanged (also a success, but NOT the denominator); RED is the six CLIENT DEFECTS (duplicate_slot_id, slot_id_out_of_range, pinned_sender_id_zero, pinned_sender_id_out_of_range, media_kind_unsupported - a VIDEO_SCREEN slot, and would_publish_and_receive_nothing - a redeclaration that would leave a receive-only participant receiving nothing: REFUSED, previous declaration kept, a refusal not a success). YELLOW is media_kind_unspecified, whose likeliest producer is a VERSION-SKEWED client whose AUDIO=0 decodes as unspecified - correlate with a client rollout, not with a forgotten field. ORANGE is declaration_budget_exhausted - a client re-declaring past MC_MAX_RECEIVE_CAPABILITY_DECLARATIONS on one connection; any occurrence is a client bug or an attack (since story 2 an accepted distinct declaration is a meeting-wide structural change, which is why the budget exists). Over-cap is NOT here: since story 3 MC-A each kind is truncated to its own cap and the excess slots read unavailable on Slot States (slot_count_over_cap is retired; there is no truncation counter). A join-carried declaration that fails the parser is ALSO counted on MC Overview's join failures as receive_capability_invalid - two views of one event; alert on the join series only. (slot_id_not_planned is retired in story 2: declared slots are now the assignment's input.) No meeting identifier, participant id, slot id or sender id appears as a label.
panels.title: Receive Capability Declarations by Outcome

panels.description: Send-directive compositions by disposition (ADR-0036 §5), recorded by the MEETING ACTOR on every composition - including those triggered by a peer's join, leave, declaration or mute - and only when the directive CHANGED. EMITTED MEANS COMPOSED, NOT DELIVERED: two hops follow it, each on its own series - participant mailbox CLOSED is Slot View Emissions outcome=delivery_failed, stream channel FULL is Dropped Outbound Messages payload_kind=signaling_raw. THE SUCCESS SET IS {emitted, emitted_empty_targets}, NOT {emitted}. §5 makes an empty target set a SPECIFIED success ("that means send nothing"), and it is ROUTINE: a solo participant, anyone nobody holds in a slot, anyone server-muted on every kind it publishes (story 3 MC-B: a server mute withdraws that kind's directive - per-kind withdrawals by cause are on Send Directive Withdrawals), and anyone not yet connected to a handler (or inside the connect settle window) is directed to send nothing, then re-sent a non-empty directive the moment someone holds it. 'Holds' means SHARES A CONNECTED HANDLER WITH (story 2 task 20) - not 'placed on the same handler', task 6's retired meaning. Under round-robin this was routine in every split two-person meeting; under the edge model an all-connected meeting co-locates, so the expected magnitude dropped. A directive may now carry several targets (every handler owning one of the sender's edges; Mean Send Targets per Directive). Both are GREEN and any failure predicate must read outcome!~"emitted|emitted_empty_targets" - PERMANENT, grounded in §5, unlike the temporary carve-out on Media Policy Pushes. The ALERT CLASSES are not restated here: their one home is DirectiveOutcome::alert_class() (crates/mc-service/src/media_signaling/outcome.rs, test module), pinned to the two rules by a unit test. MC-defect values PAGE (MCMediaSendDirectiveDefect; any non-zero value is a bug that fails CLOSED and recurs for the meeting's life); every other non-success value, including any value added later, WARNS (MCMediaSendDirectiveFailures). Both are drawn against their selectors on Send Directive Failures (ALERTED). WITHDRAWALS ARE HEALTHY and are never read from this panel: see Send Directive Withdrawals by Kind and Reason. The failure values are disjoint by construction: composition is sequential stages and the first failing stage returns its own value. Kind-free BY DESIGN (docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md, media_kind table): not split by media_kind - a decision, not an omission.
panels.title: Send Directives by Outcome

panels.description: The two send-directive rules' selectors (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml). 'MC defect' is MCMediaSendDirectiveDefect's positive selector (PAGE): a failure that fails CLOSED, recurs for the meeting's life and leaves the participant with no slots, so no stream-path panel can show it. 'environmental / unclassified' is MCMediaSendDirectiveFailures' negated selector (WARNING): meeting_state_unavailable, and any outcome nobody classified. Both rules fire on any occurrence in 15 minutes; any point above the red line at 0 is one. The classes' one home is DirectiveOutcome::alert_class() (outcome.rs). Withdrawals are healthy and are never read here. key_custody=operator; no identity. Kind-free BY DESIGN (docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md, media_kind table): not split by media_kind - a decision, not an omission.
panels.title: Send Directive Failures (ALERTED: defect pages, rest warns)

panels.description: Dispositions of dirty participants in the meeting actor's server-driven slot-view flush (ADR-0036 §5/§6; story 2): after a join, leave, declaration or mute the actor re-emits each affected declared participant's changed SendDirective and StreamAssignments, at most SLOT_VIEW_FLUSH_BATCH per actor turn. THIS DOES NOT PARTITION EMISSIONS - a participant deferred on three turns and sent on the fourth counts four times. SUCCESS SET {sent, deferred}: GREEN sent, BLUE deferred - deferred is the ROUTINE shape of the bound under load (the view is carried, coalesced and never dropped), NOT a failure. FAILURE PREDICATE, stated positively on purpose: outcome=~"delivery_failed|composition_failed" - a later value defaults to not-a-failure. RED composition_failed is an MC DEFECT (any non-zero is a bug; the stage is on Send Directives, which is the alerting home - do not alert on both). ORANGE delivery_failed is environmental: the participant actor was gone. No meeting, participant, slot or sender identity is a label.
panels.title: Slot View Emissions by Outcome

panels.description: A NON-ZERO signaling_raw RATE HERE AGAINST A HEALTHY emitted RATE ON SEND DIRECTIVES IS THE SPECIFIC SHAPE OF 'MC COMPOSED A SEND DIRECTIVE THE CLIENT NEVER RECEIVED' - emitted means COMPOSED, not delivered, and this panel is the stream-channel-FULL half of what happened next. The participant-mailbox-CLOSED half is Slot View Emissions outcome=delivery_failed - an EARLIER hop, disjoint from this one. EVERY DROP IS COUNTED; ONLY THE FIRST IS LOGGED PER CONNECTION - a wedged channel drops one message per roster broadcast, so a single WARN line can stand for thousands of drops and log volume badly understates drop volume. Take the magnitude from this graph, never from a grep. mc_participant_outbound_messages_dropped_total: the client did not receive something MC decided to send, because its outbound channel was full or closed. Deliberately NOT a fourth actor_type on mc_messages_dropped_total, which is the INBOUND mailbox path - mixing them would corrupt the topk on the cross-service errors dashboard. (mc_media_unmatched_plan_slots_total, formerly the other half of this panel, is RETIRED in story 2: plans are derived from declared slots, so it was identically zero.) Zero is healthy: a flat line at zero means no such events occurred. An ABSENT series is NOT a zero — it means the metrics pipeline is broken (recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label), not that no events occurred. This panel is not a liveness signal (read the service's traffic/overview panels for liveness), and any non-zero value warrants investigation via the service runbook.
panels.title: Dropped Outbound Messages

panels.description: Refusal REPLIES withheld by a path's reply limiter, by surface (client_mute | server_mute | unmute_request | capability; client_mute added by MC-B, unmute_request 2026-10-25: the replies to a refused client MuteRequest / UnmuteRequest). EXPECTED EMPTY - a legitimate client never reaches a reply burst, so zero is healthy and the series is present at zero from process start (absent = pipeline fault, not calm). NOT a refusal count: every refusal is counted on its own path (Server Mute Requests outcome=not_permitted|unknown_target, Mute Requests Rejected, or a Receive Capability rejection) whether or not the reply went out. EVERY suppressed reply is counted here; only the FIRST is logged per connection, so a single WARN does not mean a single suppression. Non-zero: some connection is looping refused requests (an SDK bug, or a probe). No alert: client-inflatable by construction.
panels.title: Suppressed Refusal Replies

panels.description: Mute-family requests REFUSED WHOLE for their kind list (story 3 MC-B; widened 2026-10-25, ADR-0036 §5 amendment of that date), by surface (client_mute: a participant's MuteRequest; server_mute: a ServerMuteRequest; unmute_request: an UnmuteRequest) and reason (no_kind_named: the kind list is empty; media_kind_unspecified: an UNSPECIFIED or unknown kind; duplicate_kind: one kind named twice; not_published: a named kind the subject does not publish - VIDEO_SCREEN included on all three surfaces). KIND-FREE on purpose: a refused request applied no kind, and it never reaches a per-kind cell of Mute Requests by Outcome or Server Mute Requests, nor Unmute Requests, so every mute-family request lands in exactly one home. media_kind_unsupported is NOT a reason here (it stays a capability outcome). ORDER: client_mute and unmute_request are decided on the connection before any token or actor hop; on server_mute authority is checked FIRST and the shape reasons are counted here for ANY requester, host or not (so Server Mute Requests not_permitted undercounts non-hosts by exactly those), while not_published is decided by the meeting actor after the target lookup (hosts only; it answers the same reply as an unknown target). DATED 2026-10-25: not_published moved here from Mute Requests by Outcome (where the published kind still applied); unmute and server-mute refusals of unpublished kinds are new. EXPECTED EMPTY given both preconditions - the stock SDK names only kinds it publishes (on unmute only server-muted ones) and web-app offers no host control for a NOT_PUBLISHED kind - so non-zero means an SDK regression or a probe. The series is zero-initialised as the 3 x 4 cross product: zero is healthy, and an ABSENT series is a pipeline fault, not calm. CLIENT-INFLATABLE: never a ratio denominator; no alert by decision.
panels.title: Mute Requests Rejected (by surface, reason)

panels.description: Slot states MC conveys to subscribers (ADR-0036 §6), one increment per declared slot per StreamAssignments the actor actually SENDS. The bucketed slot-state signal §11 mandates, joined to NO identity: it answers how many and how bad; MC's own assignment state answers WHO. There is no per-slot series and must not be one. The label domain mirrors the wire enum EXHAUSTIVELY (every named SlotState variant, not only the ones reachable today) so it stays comparable with the client's distribution and so an UNSPECIFIED on the wire is visible rather than absent. EMISSIONS ARE CLIENT- AND SERVER-DRIVEN since story 2: the actor re-emits on a PEER's join, leave, declaration or mute change (either kind since story 3), so the distribution is weighted by meeting churn as well as by any one client - normalise before building a ratio. fewer_sources_than_slots is every declared-but-unfilled slot - a solo participant (loopback removed, R-3), any meeting smaller than N, and every slot of a participant not yet connected to a handler; it is the healthy steady state of a small meeting. Emitted since story 3 MC-A: active (audio names the sender; live video names none), avatar_no_video (a video slot whose occupant publishes no video - precedence over any mute), avatar_client_muted, avatar_server_muted (server wins), fewer_sources_than_slots, and unavailable (truncated by that kind's cap - the over-cap signal; every video slot when MC_MAX_VIDEO_RECEIVE_SLOTS=0). Story 2's source_muted LEFT the domain with its wire value (deleted and reserved by MC-B, 2026-10-23): it is absent, not flat, and no query selects it. source_unreachable stays UNEMITTED under the story-2 edge model: a participant the subscriber shares NO connected handler with is named in unreachable_sender_ids instead (the state is reserved for a PINNED source with no shared handler, which static fill cannot produce) (see Unreachable Senders Named); a non-zero red line here is therefore an MC defect, as is unspecified. zero_requested is gone: the proto reserved it 2026-10-13 as unemittable. withheld_by_congestion arrives with the MH slot-state notification and switch_pending with §7 switching. Split by media_kind (story 3): audio and video slots have different healthy distributions (avatar_no_video exists only on video). Unreachable senders are NOT a slot state here: read Unreachable Senders Named (mc_media_unreachable_senders_total), never this counter. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Slot States by Kind

panels.description: NO SLOT-OCCUPANCY GAUGE EXISTS, SO THIS IS NOT 'slots used / cap' AND MUST NOT BE READ AS ONE. MC publishes no count of filled receive slots: mc_media_slot_states_total counts slot states CONVEYED (one per declared slot per StreamAssignments sent) and mc_media_receive_slot_cap is a config echo. What this panel shows instead - the honest substitute, not the requested ratio: LEFT AXIS, the share of conveyed slot states that carried a source (active, avatar_no_video, avatar_client_muted or avatar_server_muted) out of all conveyed. unavailable and fewer_sources_than_slots are NOT filled. Emission-weighted, so a meeting with churn weighs more than a quiet one (see Slot States). A low share is the healthy steady state of meetings with fewer other participants than the declared N (fewer_sources_than_slots - every solo participant included, since loopback is removed, R-3); it is not a fault. RIGHT AXIS, the published per-kind caps (mc_media_receive_slot_cap, publishing MC_MAX_AUDIO_RECEIVE_SLOTS / MC_MAX_VIDEO_RECEIVE_SLOTS from the ClientMediaConfig field every declaration is truncated against): the bound each kind's declared N is truncated to. A cap below the clients' N shows as unavailable on Slot States (excess slots are truncated, never rejected), and lowers the filled share here. The pair says whether declared slots are being filled and against which configured bound clients declare; it CANNOT say how close any meeting is to the cap. That reading needs an occupancy gauge that does not exist today. Guarded: the '> 0' on the conveyed total makes a window with no emissions read as no data rather than NaN; empty is healthy when no StreamAssignments were sent. key_custody=operator. No meeting, participant, slot or sender identity is on either series. Caps per media_kind (story 3): both kinds are published; a video reading of 0 confirms the R-26 video-off lever applied - max() without by(media_kind) would hide it. The filled share is computed PER media_kind (story 3 OBS-B fix: it previously summed both kinds and was plotted against per-kind caps). 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.

targets.expr:
sum by (media_kind, content_kind) (rate(mc_media_slot_states_total{slot_state=~"active|avatar_no_video|avatar_client_muted|avatar_server_muted"}[$__rate_interval]))
/
sum by (media_kind, content_kind) (rate(mc_media_slot_states_total[$__rate_interval]))
and
sum by (media_kind, content_kind) (rate(mc_media_slot_states_total[$__rate_interval])) > 0

panels.title: Receive Slot Fill vs Cap

panels.description: The configured per-kind caps MC_MAX_AUDIO_RECEIVE_SLOTS (audio) and MC_MAX_VIDEO_RECEIVE_SLOTS (video), published at boot from the SAME ClientMediaConfig field every declaration is truncated against and JoinResponse tags 13/14 carry. Read once at startup: a change applies after the MC restart, and live slot vectors are never re-truncated. A CONFIG ECHO, NOT A UTILISATION GAUGE - there is no numerator; do not build a 'slots used / cap' ratio. Receive Slot Fill vs Cap reads the nearest honest substitute beside it. Read beside Slot States: a rising unavailable with a cap below the clients' configured N is a configuration mismatch (R-1: excess slots truncated, never rejected), not a client bug. Per media_kind: a video reading of 0 confirms the R-26 video-off lever applied - max() without by(media_kind) would hide it. Video at 0 = the R-26 video-off lever (MC_MAX_VIDEO_RECEIVE_SLOTS=0) is applied. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Receive Slot Cap

panels.description: Roster participants named in StreamAssignments.unreachable_sender_ids - a routable participant whose CONNECTED handler set is disjoint from the subscriber's (ADR-0036 §9, story 2 R-33, task 20), summed over emitted views. A NON-ZERO RATE IS A CONNECTIVITY-DEGRADATION SIGNAL: every client is offered every handler and an all-connected meeting co-locates, so a healthy meeting emits zero here. EMISSION-WEIGHTED, NOT A POPULATION: it does NOT count who cannot reach whom (use the connectivity INFO lines and Connect Settles window_elapsed, MC runbook Scenario 18). Mean per emitted view = this / Slot View Emissions outcome=sent. Permanently zero on a single-handler deployment, by construction - because every ROUTABLE participant is on that handler and a not-yet-connected participant is never unreachable (see Not-Yet-Connected Senders). The field is a wire contract the client must render, not optional. No sender, meeting or handler identity. Kind-free BY DESIGN (mc-service.md, media_kind table): reachability is per participant, not per stream. Read beside Not-Yet-Connected Senders.
panels.title: Unreachable Senders Named

panels.description: Client MuteRequest dispositions (ADR-0036 §5). COUNTING UNIT: one increment per (request, NAMED kind) - a kind with no entry in the request's kind list means unchanged and is not counted, and the SDK names only the kind it changes. COUNTING-UNIT CHANGES, NONE A TRAFFIC CHANGE: rates roughly doubled at story 3 OBS-A (an interim that counted both kinds on every request), roughly HALVED again at MC-B (2026-10-23); from the story 3 R-15 fix (2026-10-24) every join added one applied per published kind (the SDK's post-join report); SINCE 2026-10-25 joins add nothing (the join's published_kinds carries the initial state), and not_published LEFT this panel for Mute Requests Rejected (a request naming an unpublished kind is refused WHOLE and counts nothing here) - compare against last week accordingly. A request refused for its kind list (empty, malformed, unpublished kind) is not counted here (Mute Requests Rejected). It PARTITIONS (accepted report, named kind) pairs. A kind is applied when its client state moved (LIVE <-> CLIENT_MUTED; every kind is definite from the join), which flips the stream's disposition FORWARD <-> PAUSED and re-emits. A camera button lands on media_kind="video" applied. Split by media_kind. CLIENT mute only: server mute is its own panel and must never be summed with this one (label-taxonomy.md, the action contract). THE SUCCESS SET IS {applied} (applied_no_recompose, unreachable since MC-A, was removed by MC-B) - the failure predicate is outcome=~"rate_limited|actor_unavailable", NOT outcome!="applied", which would count a routine state as a failure. GREEN applied: this kind's state changed; the meeting actor owes every OTHER participant a roster fan-out (Client Mute Fan-outs, per-meeting bound) and re-emits the changed slot view to the subscribers HOLDING this source; a failed re-emit is counted by the actor on Send Directives and on Slot View Emissions outcome=composition_failed. BLUE unchanged: THIS NAMED KIND's state did not move - either the identical repeat (no actor hop) or a named kind the actor found already in that state - not a failure. USE applied AS ANY RATIO DENOMINATOR, NOT unchanged: the no-op short-circuit runs before any actor hop, roster read or recomposition, so unchanged is client-inflatable at line rate, and a fraction-applied ratio computed over it is a number one participant can drive to zero. unchanged is exempt from the limiter on purpose - reversing that ordering would let a client spamming a steady state drain its own bucket on no-ops and suppress its next genuine toggle. ORANGE rate_limited is the visible edge of the mute-work token bucket (per connection; burst MUTE_WORK_BURST, one token refilled per MUTE_WORK_REFILL_INTERVAL_MS - both in crates/mc-service/src/webtransport/connection.rs, cited rather than restated). Client mute is the only repeatable client-driven path that puts work on the SHARED meeting actor's mailbox - one actor hop, a roster fan-out owed to the other N-1 participants (AWAITED sends; story 3 R-15 fix, 2026-10-24, reversing story-2 security S-2's removal of that fan-out), and a re-emit to the source's holders, which the actor bounds per meeting per turn (Slot View Emissions outcome=deferred); its MH re-pushes are latest-wins per handler (one in flight, one pending). THIS BUCKET BOUNDS EACH SENDER, NOT THE MEETING: N connections each within their own bucket are not bounded here. The meeting-wide bound on the roster fan-out is the per-meeting fan-out bucket (CLIENT_MUTE_FANOUT_BURST, CLIENT_MUTE_FANOUT_REFILL_INTERVAL_MS - crates/mc-service/src/actors/client_mute_fanout.rs), whose edge is Client Mute Fan-outs outcome=awaiting_token; under churn the bound DELAYS changes and never drops one (per-recipient delivery loss is Dropped Outbound Messages payload_kind=participant_update_muted, stale until the subject's next change). For 'mute indicators are slow in a big meeting', read that panel, not this one. A HUMAN NEVER REACHES THIS LIMITER, so a sustained non-zero rate means one connection is toggling far above human rates - a client-side repeat loop first, an abusive peer second - and it is bounded to that connection either way. It is a rate limit and NOT a budget on purpose: a budget would permanently freeze that participant's client-mute state once spent. A dropped report never lets media out (§5 enforces client mute at CAPTURE), but it leaves MC's view of that kind stale (PAUSED/avatar, and the client-mute indicator EVERY other participant sees) until the participant's next report of the SAME kind. RED actor_unavailable is environmental and terminal. No meeting identifier, participant id, slot id or sender id appears as a label. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Client Mute Requests by Kind and Outcome

panels.description: ServerMuteRequest dispositions by action (the verb ASKED for FOR EACH NAMED KIND: mute | unmute, never its result - {audio muted} counts only mute/audio; {audio muted, video not} counts mute/audio AND unmute/video) and outcome (story 2 task 12; ADR-0036 §5, §7). Counted SEPARATELY from client mute (Mute Requests by Outcome): different decider, enforcement point (directive withdrawal plus MH ingress drop, not client capture) and remedy. COUNTING UNIT: one increment per (request, NAMED kind); an absent kind is unchanged and not counted. Rates roughly doubled at story 3 OBS-A (interim: both kinds counted) and roughly HALVED at MC-B (2026-10-23) - counting unit, not traffic. A request refused for its kind list is counted only on Mute Requests Rejected: the shape reasons from ANY requester, host or not (so not_permitted here undercounts non-hosts by exactly those requests), and not_published - a kind the TARGET does not publish, refused WHOLE since 2026-10-25 (it used to count applied here) - for hosts only. Split by media_kind. SERVER mute only: never summed with client mute (label-taxonomy.md, the action contract). The failure predicate is POSITIVE: outcome=~"rate_limited|actor_unavailable" - do not harmonise it to outcome!="applied". not_permitted vs unknown_target: the metric distinguishes two refusals the CLIENT never can (one byte-identical wire error) - deliberate, do not harmonise. unknown_target is reachable ONLY for a host requester, because authority is checked before the target is looked up. not_permitted is CLIENT-INFLATABLE (the check precedes any actor hop) - NEVER use it in a ratio denominator and never alert on its raw rate. No alert on this panel by decision: non-zero mute is healthy moderation. Not a join key with the client's dt_client_media_mute_transitions_total{action} despite identical values. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Server Mute Requests by Kind

panels.description: Participant UnmuteRequest dispositions: a server-muted participant asking the host(s) to lift its mute. NOTIFIES ONLY - it never clears a mute (the single writer is the host's ServerMuteRequest). ONE increment per request, never per host relayed to; a per-host delivery failure is the later hop (Dropped Outbound Messages, signaling_raw), disjoint from this panel. Failure predicate, positive: outcome=~"rate_limited|actor_unavailable". not_server_muted and no_host_connected are ROUTINE (no_host_connected is normal once the host has left). not_server_muted is client-driven: keep it out of any ratio denominator. Kind-free BY DESIGN (docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md, media_kind table): not split by media_kind - a decision, not an omission.
panels.title: Unmute Requests

panels.description: How many (participant, kind) sources MC believes are SERVER-muted right now, per media_kind, summed across each MC instance's meetings (one series per instance and kind; a participant muted on both kinds is 1 on each). Since story 3 MC-A each kind's server mute reaches MH as that stream's DROP_AT_INGRESS disposition, so the SUM ACROSS KINDS is comparable with MH's server_muted drops - a STATE level, not an event rate: a mute applied yesterday is still here while Server Mute Requests stays flat. Present at zero from process start. Recomputed from live state on the controller's health walk, so it cannot drift after an actor dies. Read it against MH's server_muted drops at FLEET level only (sum across MC pods vs sum of mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="server_muted"} rate across MH pods) and DIRECTIONALLY - never divided, never per instance (MC and MH meeting sets do not nest). Since MC-B gauge > 0 with fleet drops near zero is the NORMAL shape (a server mute withdraws the directive, so a compliant client sends nothing to drop; Send Directive Withdrawals reason=server_muted is the primary evidence the mute took) - the comparison detects only a sender that ignored its empty targets. Beyond that, gauge > 0 with a flat fleet drop rate is only a candidate disagreement: a muted participant who is silent, disconnected, in grace, or does not publish the muted kind drops nothing. It does not answer whether ONE meeting has a mute in force. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Server-Muted Sources

panels.description: mc_media_client_mute_fanouts_total: the visible edge of the meeting actor's PER-MEETING bound on the client-mute ROSTER fan-out (story 3 R-15 fix, 2026-10-24; ADR-0036 §5 amendment of that date). Every applied client-mute report owes the other participants a full ParticipantMuteUpdate snapshot; the per-meeting bucket (CLIENT_MUTE_FANOUT_BURST at once, one more per CLIENT_MUTE_FANOUT_REFILL_INTERVAL_MS - crates/mc-service/src/actors/client_mute_fanout.rs) paces those fan-outs FIFO, latest-state-wins. COUNTING UNIT: one increment per SUBJECT event, NEVER per recipient - do not compare against N-1-scaled delivery counts. GREEN fanned_out (a solo participant's included, zero recipients): one subject's snapshot was COMPOSED and handed to the awaited sends to every other participant present - composed, NOT delivered (per-recipient wire loss is Dropped Outbound Messages payload_kind=participant_update_muted). YELLOW awaiting_token: one subject still pending at the end of a flush. IT DOES NOT PARTITION TRANSITIONS: it counts pending-subject-flushes - a subject waiting across k flushes counts awaiting_token k times, then fanned_out once (or nothing more if it left the meeting or a server-mute update already carried its state), and a subject toggled many times while pending is fanned out once with its latest state - so awaiting_token/fanned_out is NOT the fraction of toggles delayed. Both outcomes are success: no failure predicate, no alert. Sustained awaiting_token means the bound is DELAYING facts - peers' mute indicators LAG; the bound never drops a fact (per-recipient delivery loss is participant_update_muted, not this panel). Usage: 'mute indicators are slow in a big meeting' - non-zero awaiting_token confirms the per-meeting bound is pacing; zero rules it out (check participant_update_muted drops next). Kind-free (one fan-out carries all four controls). No meeting, participant or sender identity appears as a label. Zero is healthy for awaiting_token: a flat line at zero means no such events occurred. An ABSENT series is NOT a zero - it means the metrics pipeline is broken (recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label), not that no events occurred. This panel is not a liveness signal (read the service's traffic/overview panels for liveness).
panels.title: Client Mute Fan-outs

panels.description: Stream WITHDRAWALS (story 3 R-8): a DELIVERED SendDirective whose stream of this kind went from non-empty to EMPTY targets, by media_kind and reason. reason=unwatched (nobody holds the stream in a slot any more; emitted since MC-A) and reason=server_muted (the kind is server-muted, so its directive is withdrawn whatever its watchers; emitted since MC-B - the MC-side evidence that a server mute stopped capture, runbook Scenario 21 'camera light still on'). The reason is the CURRENT cause at delivery; a server mute of an already-unwatched stream is no transition and counts nothing, and an unmute is never counted. Counted per TRANSITION, never per re-render, and not on a reconnect's fresh view. Counted on DELIVERY, unlike Send Directives (composition): a withdrawal whose delivery failed is visible only on Slot View Emissions outcome=delivery_failed. A WITHDRAWAL IS NOT MEDIA FAILURE - nobody watching a camera is routine, and so is a host's server mute; read it beside Send Directives outcome=emitted_empty_targets. key_custody=operator. No meeting, participant, sender, slot or stream identity appears as a label. Zero is healthy: a flat line at zero means no such events occurred. An ABSENT series is NOT a zero — it means the metrics pipeline is broken (recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label), not that no events occurred. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.
panels.title: Send Directive Withdrawals by Kind and Reason

panels.description: The minimum keyframe interval MC directs on every video stream: MC_VIDEO_MIN_KEYFRAME_INTERVAL_MS / 1000 (story 3 R-23; MC's own ConfigMap mc-service-config, bounds 100..=10000 ms, default 500). A CONFIG ECHO set once at boot from the SAME validated value the video directive carries as min_keyframe_interval_ms, so published and directed values cannot drift. Configuration, NOT GoP or frame timing - the keyframe-storm alert reads it as a server-side bound, never a client-reported value. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Directed Video Minimum Keyframe Interval

panels.description: mc_session_join_failures_total{error_type} for the story 3 join-media values (all reach the client as one generic INVALID_REQUEST; only this label splits them): header_version_unsupported (an SDK lacking header version 3 - the old-bundle-meets-new-MC rollout signal; expected during a rollout, panel only), publish_kind_invalid, receive_capability_invalid, publishes_and_receives_nothing (neither publishes nor receives, judged on the declaration as sent) and reconnect_publish_set_mismatch (a reconnect presenting a different publish set). reconnect_publish_set_mismatch is NOT production-reachable today (actor-level reconnect is not wired to the WebTransport accept path), so a flat zero there is expected, not a broken series. SCOPED: this panel shows only these five error_type values, a subset of the counter; the full split (every error_type, including any added later) is MC Overview's "Session Join Failures by Type" panel, so a flat line here never means "no join refusals". Alerted only indirectly through MCHighJoinFailureRate. Zero is healthy: the counter is zero-initialised, so a flat 0 is calm and an ABSENT series is a fault (pipeline or pod), not calm.
panels.title: Join Refusals - Story 3 Media Join Values

panels.description: MH connect/disconnect notifications that did NOT become (or change) participant connectivity, by reason (story 2 task 20). Connectivity decides who hears whom, so every way a notification fails to become routing input is counted. READ PER REASON, NEVER AS ONE RATE: unknown_connection is ROUTINE (every declined connection's Disconnected); participant_unknown is a low-rate join race; user_ambiguous and meeting_unknown are faults; a SUSTAINED handler_not_in_set means an MH restarted under a new id and story-4 re-registration has not happened (stale connectivity does not self-clear, MC runbook Scenario 18); connection_bound_refused is EXPECTED-EMPTY (red); retired_connection is a Connected delivered after its own Disconnected, refused by MC's tombstone. No meeting, participant, handler or connection identity.
panels.title: MH Notifications Unapplied by Reason

panels.description: Participants' connectivity episodes settling (story 2 task 20). PER EPISODE, so it IS a population: window_elapsed counts participants that did NOT reach every handler of their meeting within MC_MEDIA_CONNECT_SETTLE_MS - Scenario 18 Step 0's count of 'who failed to connect everywhere'. complete = reached every handler (settles at its last connect, no added latency). The window withholds routing while a participant establishes (no edges, not unreachable); window_elapsed is the visible edge of that mask. Read against Connect Settle Window.
panels.title: Connect Settles by Outcome

panels.description: Roster members NOT routable (not yet connected to any handler, inside their settle window, or re-establishing) counted per emitted StreamAssignments, the subscriber ITSELF INCLUDED (so a subscriber's own all-fewer_sources view, identical to a small meeting's, is not invisible). The partner of Unreachable Senders Named: that one is silence because connected sets are disjoint, this one is silence because someone is not connected yet. NOT EXPECTED-EMPTY - every join passes through it; PERSISTENCE, not rate, is the fault. Emission-weighted: normalise by Slot View Emissions outcome=sent. Mixes the subscriber's own contribution (at most 1) with its peers'. Kind-free BY DESIGN (docs/observability/metrics/mc-service.md, media_kind table): not split by media_kind - a decision, not an omission.
panels.title: Not-Yet-Connected Senders

panels.description: Send targets per emitted SendDirective (story 2 task 20): a sender sends to every handler owning one of its edges, and MC's edge policy co-locates to minimise that. ~1 when participants reach every handler; above 1 only with genuinely partial connectivity. A sustained rise with healthy connectivity means co-location degraded - visible otherwise only as client uplink cost. Changed directives only (the emitted boundary). Story 3: targets are counted per stream by kind and are split by kind here; the DENOMINATOR stays kind-free on purpose (a directive is composed per participant, before any stream exists), joined with ignoring(media_kind, content_kind) group_left. The two kinds' lines sum to the old all-kind ratio. 2026-10-26 - SERIES IDENTITY, NOT TRAFFIC: every per-kind MC series co-carries content_kind (main until screen share ships; label-taxonomy.md query rule), so this panel groups and selects both kind labels and screen share will appear as its own video/screen line, never folded into the camera's. At rollout the per-kind series start new: rate() ramps on them - expected, not an incident.

targets.expr: sum by (media_kind, content_kind) (rate(mc_media_send_targets_total[$__rate_interval])) / ignoring(media_kind, content_kind) group_left() sum(rate(mc_media_send_directives_total{outcome="emitted"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: Mean Send Targets per Directive

panels.description: Publisher->subscriber edges that changed handler between two renders (story 2 task 20). connectivity_change is routine: the edge's handler left one party's connected set and the edge moved, keeping its slot and sender. unexpected is EXPECTED-EMPTY and RED: an edge moved while both parties were still on its old handler - an edge-stability invariant violation; capture and escalate (ERROR at mc.actor.meeting names both handlers). Detected by diffing consecutive renders, independently of the code it checks.
panels.title: Edge Moves by Reason

panels.description: The connect settle window this MC enforces (MC_MEDIA_CONNECT_SETTLE_MS), published from the SAME field the meeting actors enforce. A CONFIG ECHO. Cost it names: time-to-first-audio for a participant that does not reach every handler is delayed by up to this; it never appears in join latency (which stops at the JoinResponse). Read Connect Settles window_elapsed against it.
panels.title: Connect Settle Window

panels.description: Age of the OLDEST un-rotated departure across live meetings (mc_meeting_kek_rotation_pending_age_seconds; a MAXIMUM, refreshed every KEK_GAUGE_REFRESH_INTERVAL in crates/mc-service/src/media_admission/rotation.rs from times the meeting actors recorded, so a wedged actor still ages), beside W itself (mc_meeting_kek_rotation_window_seconds, publishing MC_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS) and the overdue threshold (mc_meeting_kek_rotation_overdue_threshold_seconds, W x KEK_ROTATION_OVERDUE_MULTIPLIER). MCKekRotationOverdue pages when pending age exceeds the overdue-threshold GAUGE - gauge vs gauge, no literal; its `for` duration lives in the rule (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml). Healthy: a sawtooth that climbs to about W and drops to 0 at each rotation, never reaching the threshold. While pending age is above zero, a departed participant still holds a working KEK: this is a confidentiality exposure window, not a media-quality one. Pending age is cleared AT ROTATION, not when every push succeeds - undelivered pushes are the KEK Push Outcomes panel. Rotations by trigger are on MC Overview's Meeting KEK Issuance by Trigger panel.
panels.title: KEK Rotation Pending Age vs Overdue Threshold

panels.description: One MeetingKekUpdate outcome per rostered recipient per rotation (ADR-0036 Sec 4). delivered = handed to the connection's outbound stream (not a client ack). participant_gone = rostered but no live connection (reconnect grace) - BENIGN, it gets the current KEK on return. dropped_outbound = outbound channel full or closed. actor_unavailable = participant actor exited or its mailbox closed (MCActorPanic territory). timed_out = no answer within KEK_PUSH_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT (crates/mc-service/src/media_admission/rotation.rs; read mc_actor_mailbox_depth; MCHighMailboxDepthCritical territory). Every non-delivered, non-gone push is a security residual: that member never rotates its own transmit keys, so a departed participant keeps opening THAT member's media past W. MCKekPushFailureRate fires on the outcome!~"delivered|participant_gone" share; its threshold and duration live in the rule (infra/docker/prometheus/rules/mc-alerts.yaml) and are not restated here.
panels.title: KEK Push Outcomes

panels.description: Time from the rotation decision to the LAST per-recipient push outcome - the window in which some members hold the new key and others do not. Bounded above by the per-push outcome timeout KEK_PUSH_OUTCOME_TIMEOUT (crates/mc-service/src/media_admission/rotation.rs), which the top bucket covers. The p99 tail matters most: it is the portion that can overlap the next rotation.
panels.title: KEK Rotation Duration

panels.description: How many roster removals each leave-triggered rotation covered. The debounce is measured from the OLDEST un-rotated departure and never reset by a later one, so a busy meeting coalesces several departures into one rotation per W. Observed for participant_left rotations only.
panels.title: KEK Departures Coalesced per Rotation

panels.description: Rotations that could not be performed; the KEK was left UNCHANGED. Zero is healthy. While this is non-zero every departed participant keeps a working KEK (the W bound is SUSPENDED, not delayed) and MCKekRotationOverdue pages. rng is the live arm (CSPRNG failure, retried after W). generation_exhausted is permanent for the meeting (u16 KEK generation at its ceiling - u16 generations x the W floor MIN_KEK_ROTATION_DEBOUNCE_SECONDS in crates/mc-service/src/config.rs, i.e. weeks of uninterrupted rotation) and the page will not clear until the meeting ends.
panels.title: KEK Rotation Failures

panels.description: The highest sender_id namespace consumption across live meetings, in the CURRENT epoch - cursor consumption including ids skipped by an epoch reset's exclusion snapshot, so NOT a count of admissions and not comparable to a join count. Resets at each epoch. When the u16 namespace is exhausted (NonZeroU16, anchored to KEY_ID_SENDER_ID_BITS in crates/mc-service/src/media_admission/sender_id.rs) MC rotates the KEK and reissues from a fresh namespace (sender_space_exhausted on the issuance panel); the meeting keeps admitting. A high value means a flapping client or a scripted join loop: flapper eviction does not ship, and this is its visibility. Deliberately no alert.
panels.title: Sender ID Namespace Consumption (max)

panels.description: Verdicts MC returned for per-(meeting, handler) heartbeats (story 4 MC-B1). owned is the healthy steady state. released_removed = RELEASED(removal trigger): a zombie or a lost EndMeeting being fenced. released_ended = no meeting actor, RELEASED(MEETING_ENDED): the lost-EndMeeting retry rate. released_unassigned (misroute) and owner_mismatch (the heartbeat's mc_id is not this MC: FAILED_PRECONDITION) are expected ZERO - any increase is a contract or routing defect. No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Verdicts by Outcome

panels.description: Inter-arrival of ACCEPTED heartbeats per (meeting, handler); stale or replayed arrivals are excluded (they show on Handler Applied-Sequence Lag). Healthy is about N/3 (the interval MC sends MH); the deadline line is N (MC_MH_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS, mc_media_handler_heartbeat_deadline_seconds). Buckets are derived from N. A p95 approaching N means heartbeats are being lost or delayed; MC-B2 declares a handler Dead past N.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Inter-Arrival vs Deadline

panels.description: Sent minus applied policy_generation per OWNED heartbeat (stale ones included), per (meeting, handler) - replaces the retired pod-level divergence gauge. 0 is healthy; a sustained non-zero p95 is a handler that is not keeping up with MC's pushes (MC-B2: Lagging, then Impaired). Not observed while MC has never pushed to a pair, nor when MH reports a generation ahead of what MC sent (counted on Handler Heartbeat Anomalies instead). Integer buckets.
panels.title: Handler Applied-Sequence Lag

panels.description: Connections a heartbeat retired from MC's state (remove-only reconcile, ADR-0039 §6): one per distinct (handler, connection_id) across connectivity keys and binding-ledger entries. Each is a lost NotifyParticipantDisconnected the heartbeat healed. Sustained non-zero means the MH->MC notification path is lossy. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Connected-Set Corrections

panels.description: Heartbeats MC answered but could not fully use, counted on every heartbeat carrying the anomaly. Expected zero in production; in the dev cluster the env-test Injection fixture produces applied_ahead_of_sent by design. connection_ids_over_cap / connection_id_malformed: an MH contract or version-skew fault; the verdict and liveness still applied, only that heartbeat's reconcile was skipped (skipping only keeps connections). applied_ahead_of_sent: MH reported a generation MC never sent (an out-of-band writer, a forgery or a version skew) - liveness still applies but the watermark is clamped to what MC sent (story 4 MC-B2), no lag reading. apply_refused_invalid / apply_refused_transport_inconsistent: MH refused MC's PENDING policy as malformed - an MC CONTRACT FAULT (ERROR log), never a declaration or replacement; a refusal while MC's policy is installed is not counted. WARNING candidate (OBS-ALERTS).
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Anomalies by Reason

panels.description: N, the heartbeat timeout this MC enforces (MC_MH_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_MS), published from the SAME value the RegisterMeeting interval (floor(N/3), min 1 ms) and the intake derive from. A CONFIG ECHO. Read it beside MH's QUIC idle timeout: the client-loss evidence is interpretable only when the two are about equal.
panels.title: Handler Heartbeat Deadline (N)

panels.description: (meeting, handler) pairs declared Dead (heartbeat_timeout: no accepted heartbeat for longer than N after the first confirmed RegisterMeeting) or Impaired (apply_lag: applied generation behind what MH owes for longer than L = 2N, or a STREAM_CEILING / EDGE_CAP refusal) and REMOVED from the meeting (story 4 MC-B2). Per (meeting, handler): one MH death is one declaration per affected meeting. No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Declarations by Trigger

panels.description: Evidence start -> declaration, p50/p95 per trigger over the SELECTED dashboard range (rate(...[$__range]); a quantile is scale-free, so this is the quantile of every declaration in the range) - declarations are rare, so a per-interval timeseries would be empty when it is read after an incident; set the range to cover the incident. heartbeat_timeout starts at the last accepted heartbeat (or the first confirmed RegisterMeeting); apply_lag starts at the lag onset (or the refusing heartbeat for a capacity refusal). Buckets derived from N (N/2 .. 4N): expect heartbeat_timeout just past N and lag-held apply_lag just past L = 2N. Shown beside N. Durations are observed, never gated. Absent until the first declaration (a histogram cannot be zero-initialised).
panels.title: Handler Detection Time by Trigger vs N (selected range)

panels.description: How a lag suspicion ended: declared (Lagging -> Impaired) vs cleared (Lagging -> caught up). Lag is judged against the generation owed since the PREVIOUS heartbeat, so a push racing one heartbeat is not a suspicion. A high cleared rate is the near-miss / N-tuning signal. Lagging -> Dead and refusal-driven Impaired are not counted here.
panels.title: Lag Suspicions by Outcome

panels.description: Meetings on each MC whose handler set is EMPTY after a removal ('awaiting handler', ADR-0039 §3). A meeting whose only handler is still Registering does not count. Recompute-and-set from the census on the controller's health walk. MC keeps acquiring a replacement from GC with bounded, jittered backoff and the meeting recovers by itself on a later grant (story 4 MC-C; see Handler Replacement). Alert: OBS-ALERTS' MCMediaMeetingsAwaitingHandler (not in this release).
panels.title: Meetings Without Handlers

panels.description: The ONE EndMeeting(cause) a removal sends the removed handler, after draining its push worker; never retried - the retry is its next heartbeat, answered RELEASED (Handler Heartbeat Verdicts, released_removed). unavailable_exhausted is the EXPECTED outcome after a crash, which is why this is not mc_media_end_meeting_total (whose failure alert means an ended meeting leaked). No alert.
panels.title: Removal Releases by Trigger and Outcome

panels.description: MediaHandlerSet messages delivered to participants per second, by reason (story 4 MC-D). join = the (re)joiner's own set; change = a handler-membership change (version advanced); failed_report = the credential re-push a client's FAILED report for an in-set ref triggers (sender only, per-session limited); token_refresh = the TTL/3 media_dial refresh (version and refs unchanged). token_refresh should track connected participants / (TTL/3); its absence while participants are connected means the refresh is broken. Counted at successful enqueue: drops are mc_participant_outbound_messages_dropped_total{payload_kind="media_handler_set"}. No meeting, participant, handler or ref label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Set Pushes by Reason

panels.description: The media_dial token lifetime this MC mints with (MC_MEDIA_DIAL_TOKEN_TTL_SECONDS, [60, 900]) and the NOMINAL per-participant refresh interval TTL/3, both published from the SAME value the mint and the scheduler read. CONFIG ECHOES, per instance. Each participant's actual refresh is jittered EARLIER by up to a tenth of the interval, never later.
panels.title: Dial Credential TTL / Refresh Interval

panels.description: Replacement ACQUISITION ATTEMPTS by outcome (story 4 MC-C): one AcquireMediaHandler call, or one owed replacement refused at the per-meeting attempt bound (rate_limited). NOT a migration count: a migration that retries contributes one no_capacity / gc_unavailable per failed attempt and at most one completed; a minimum-interval deferral is never counted. admission_refused = the grant was removed before its first RegisterMeeting ack (registration failed after retries, OR declared Dead/Impaired while still Registering). Per-migration completion = completed / declarations (trigger != planned_transfer). apply_lag includes a handler whose FIRST RegisterMeeting never acked. timed_out is planned_transfer only (MC-F). No meeting, handler or connection label. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Handler Migration Attempts by Trigger and Outcome

panels.description: p95 of each migration phase (story 4 MC-C): replacement = removal -> GC grant (includes every retry), registration = grant -> first RegisterMeeting ack (Active), reconnect = Active -> every participant admitted at that moment (and still present) is MH-reported connected to it. Buckets derive from config (settle window, the backoff ladder, the registration bound, the retry budget). Compare the replacement phase with the Replacement Pacing stat.
panels.title: Handler Migration Phase Duration p95 by Phase

panels.description: The per-meeting minimum interval between replacement attempts (MC_MH_REPLACEMENT_MIN_INTERVAL_MS, also the backoff ladder's first step), the ladder cap (MC_MH_REPLACEMENT_BACKOFF_MAX_MS) and the DERIVED replacement retry budget (ladder to its first capped step + one capped step + the push worker's initial-registration bound). CONFIG ECHOES, per instance. The awaiting-handler page bound (MCMediaMeetingsAwaitingHandler) derives from the budget, never a literal.
panels.title: Replacement Pacing and Retry Budget
